checks: Verified source 4c405e76fb81c248 §§4–6 and formulas (6)–(8) against its frozen source hash. The paired-roof condition in §6 follows immediately from the stated upper bound h≤min_D g.

The lower bound on h places the reflected lower roof 2h−g(−X) above −L, and the upper bound places h below each g(X), giving ordered slab heights. Also h≥−L and h≤g(0), so (0,h) is an actual point over the integer base zero.

The involution (X,t)→(−X,2h−t) preserves the sampled lattice and the summed fiber area. The slab mass is 2(Q−hW) by Fubini and invariance of ν. For a containing closed halfspace, its indicator plus the reflected indicator is at least one pointwise, including for a pure base normal with boundary fibers. The flat upper cap has mass Q−hW, including at both interval endpoints, which proves exact attainment.

The t=0 section is D. Pair reflection gives raw section depth at least W/2 at zero, and the complementary continuous-coordinate halfspaces each have mass W/2 because their common trace is ν-null. At least one contains any section mark, so the maximum normalized section depth equals 1/2.

Each positive-area sampled fiber corresponds to a positive-length D fiber since L+g is positive and bounded. An interior point of that section interval with t=0 lies in the interior of the original fiber, proving a proper cut. The ratio Q/(LW+Q) tends to zero, and the lower cylinder centered at (0,−L/2) gives the claimed competitor once L>2Q/W.

Independently integrated the rational example using exact fractions. The bases are −1,0,1 and each fiber contributes 2 to W, 5/2 to Q, and 6 below t=0. Thus W=6, Q=15/2, lower mass=18, and total=51/2. The minimum and maximum roof heights are 1/4 and 9/4, giving the interval [−3/8,1/4] and raw endpoint depths 39/4 and 6. The normalized zero-height depth is 5/17.
The positive s half-interval contributes total section length 3, upper mass 9/4 and lower mass 9. Hence the captured fractions are 1/2, 3/10 and 1/2, respectively.
